Currently, this area feels very lacking to me in multiple ways:

  • For parsing, we have OfScientific instance, but it goes through a possibly large Nat, which can be undesirable in some scenarios. Also, we don't have any function that parses a String directly to a Float.
  • For printing, we have ToString instance, but it just calls C++ std::to_string which is lossy, and cannot be used for alternative formats (manually choosing between fixed/scientific notation, and setting precision). Batteries.Float.toStringFull exists, but it can't help with formatting either.

One idea is to incorporate a 3rd-party library like ryu (https://github.com/ulfjack/ryu) to help with these. I suggest ryu specifically because:

  • it has both parsing and printing functionalities
  • on printing, it generates the shortest possible lossless representation, and supports fixed and scientific output with precision
  • its correctness is proven and the algorithm is already used in many other languages
  • it is Apache-2.0/Boost-1.0 licensed
